question: Which of the following is a group of chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and primarily aquatic (both freshwater and marine) organisms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Algae**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Algae** are a diverse group of chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic organisms.
 
• They are primarily **aquatic**, found in both freshwater and marine environments.
 
• Algae are capable of **photosynthesis** and produce oxygen as a byproduct.
 
• They play a crucial role in aquatic ecosystems as **primary producers**.
 
• Algae can vary in size from microscopic **phytoplankton** to large seaweeds like kelp.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chlorophyll**

 
 
• Chlorophyll is the green pigment found in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria.
 
• It is essential for photosynthesis, allowing plants to absorb light energy from the sun.
 
• There are several types of chlorophyll, with chlorophyll-a being the most common in algae.
 
 
 
• **Thalloid**
 
 
• The term "thalloid" refers to the simple, undifferentiated body structure of certain plants and algae.
 
• Unlike higher plants, thalloid organisms do not have roots, stems, or leaves.
 
• Examples include liverworts and certain types of algae.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis**
 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants and some other organisms use sunlight to synthesize foods with the help of chlorophyll.
 
• It involves the transformation of carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.
 
• This process is fundamental to the survival of life on Earth, providing the primary energy source for all living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Aquatic Ecosystems**
 
 
• Aquatic ecosystems include both freshwater and marine environments where algae are commonly found.
 
• These ecosystems are vital for the global carbon cycle and support a diverse range of organisms.
 
• Algae serve as the foundation of the food web in aquatic ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Phytoplankton**
 
 
• Phytoplankton are microscopic algae that float in the water column of oceans and freshwater bodies.
 
• They are primary producers, forming the base of the aquatic food chain.
 
• Phytoplankton produce a significant portion of the Earth's oxygen through photosynthesis.
